title: Surge window cluster inventory and weekly utilization snapshot
content:
Purpose: quick-reference spreadsheet-style export for the most recent 7-day surge window (UTC) focusing on clusters and pools that crossed 75% sustained utilization. This is intended for capacity planners and SRE on-call to identify short-term reserve targets and pools for temporary throttling or preferential routing.

Notes:
- Data pulled from gpu-metrics-rollup job (agg window = 5m) and aggregated by UTC date; rollup timestamp 2026-04-10T23:50Z for the week ending 2026-04-10.
- 'Headroom' is computed as (available_vgpus - reserved_peak_vgpus) / total_vgpus; reserved_peak_vgpus = 95th percentile of concurrent vgpu usage per pool over window.
- 'Incidents' column references any PagerDuty or active SLO alerts overlapping the day.

CSV rows (date,cluster,pool,region,avg_util_pct,p95_util_pct,peak_vgpu_count,total_vgpus,headroom_pct,incidents,notes):
2026-04-04,cluster-eu-2,pool-inference-high,eu-west1,68.4,91.2,42,64,34.4,PD-421,short bursts from customer-42 nightly retraining
2026-04-04,cluster-na-3,pool-dedicated-batch,us-central1,54.9,78.1,31,48,35.4,,steady background batch jobs; small headroom erosion mid-day
2026-04-05,cluster-apac-1,pool-shared-low,asia-south1,39.1,60.2,12,32,62.5,,low overall; occasional spikes due to ci/test bursts
2026-04-06,cluster-eu-2,pool-inference-high,eu-west1,72.7,95.6,45,64,29.7,PD-423,peak after model-rollout v1.14; KV cache warm-up increased token volume
2026-04-07,cluster-na-1,pool-preemptible-surge,us-east4,81.3,99.1,53,64,17.2,PD-425,shortfall vs SLO; autoscaler delayed under sustained ramp
2026-04-08,cluster-na-3,pool-dedicated-batch,us-central1,61.8,85.0,41,48,14.6,,later-night backlog flushes
2026-04-09,cluster-eu-1,pool-embeddings,eu-west2,48.7,66.3,22,40,45.0,,steady with predictable diurnal pattern

Quick takeaways:
- Two clusters (cluster-eu-2 and cluster-na-1) hit >90% p95 utilization during the week and show low headroom (<30%). These are candidates for immediate reserve reallocation or emergency burst capacity.
- pool-preemptible-surge (us-east4) is repeatedly saturating on peak; autoscaler documentation shows a 3-minute cool-down which is too slow for the observed ramp pattern.
- pool-inference-high (eu-west1) spikes correlate with model rollouts; recommend rolling back or enabling canary split traffic to inference-medium until kv-cache warm-up completes.

Short-term (next 72 hours) recommended actions:
- Temporarily increase reserved_vgpus on cluster-na-1 and cluster-eu-2 by 12 vGPUs each (ENG-1629).
- Add a 30s fast-scale path to the autoscaler for pools with label "burst-sensitive=true" and lower cooldown to 30s for a trial on pool-preemptible-surge. Tagging PR: github.com/redwood/infra/PR-874.
- Configure routing policy: route non-SLO-critical rerank/embedding traffic to cluster-eu-1 during predicted surge windows (22:00-02:00 UTC) for eu-west customers.

Queries and checks to reproduce data quickly:
- rollup query (promql): sum by (cluster,pool) (max_over_time(gpu_vgpu_in_use[5m])) / sum by(cluster,pool) (gpu_vgpu_capacity) * 100 for range 7d
- headroom check: select cluster,pool,percentile(usage,95) as p95 from gpu_usage_5m where ts >= '2026-04-03' and ts < '2026-04-10' group by cluster,pool
- check incidents: jira filter "project = INF and created >= '2026-04-03' and labels in (gpu,surge)"

Follow-ups for planning cycle (T+2 weeks):
- Capacity plan: consider adding 1 additional 8-GPU server to eu-west1 pool or convert 16 legacy preemptibles to 8xA10 dedicated units based on cost-vs-headroom analysis.
- Run synthetic workload with KV cache warm-up flag enabled to measure 30-min post-rollout delta; attach results to the rollout runbook.

Comments / open questions (notes to SRE lead):
- Is the 95th percentile reserved policy still appropriate for pools with heavy burstiness? Might move to p99 for critical pools.
- Any known customers on cluster-na-1 with guaranteed SLAs that we should notify before temporary scaling?

Attachments referenced in this sheet: weekly-surge-windows-plot.png (exported from dashboards), cluster-eu-2-kv-warmup-trace-2026-04-06.log

Author notes: this is a compact sheet intended for fast triage. For full dashboard exports see linked artifact above. Update the CSV rows if you re-run rollup with alternative window sizes; keep a copy in the capacity-runbook folder.
